study_identification_part.si4_title: Brain charts for the human lifespan

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The introduction explicitly states the aim to assemble an open resource of normative brain charts based on the largest possible MRI dataset and to use centile scores to quantify individual differences, including clinical applications such as detecting neuroanatomical variation across disorders.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: “Here we assemble an interactive open resource to benchmark brain morphology derived from any current or future sample of MRI data…we aggregated 123,984 MRI scans…MRI metrics were quantified by centile scores…Brain charts identified previously…neuroanatomical variation across neurological and psychiatric disorders.”

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: They note aggregating 123,984 scans from >100 studies (101,457 participants) across the lifespan and refer to Supplementary Tables for demographics, and mention image quality control using expert visual curation plus automated metrics. However, explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria for healthy controls and detailed exclusion reasons are not described in the main text.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “we aggregated 123,984 MRI scans, across more than 100 primary studies, from 101,457 human participants between 115 days post-conception to 100 years of age…Demographics for each cross-sectional sample of healthy controls included in the reference dataset…are detailed in Supplementary Table 1.2-1.8…image quality control, which used a combination of expert visual curation and automated metrics of image quality (Supplementary Information 2)”

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The modelling was sex-stratified, age was modelled with fractional polynomials, and study/site and preprocessing pipeline were included as random or fixed effects to address batch effects.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: “We used GAMLSS…to estimate…separately for males and females, allowing for random effects…study-specific offsets…were also modelled as random effects…age, preprocessing pipeline and study were each included in the GAMLSS model estimation…”

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: They describe aggregating MRI data from over 100 primary studies and direct readers to Supplementary Information 19 for descriptions of all contributing datasets, including open MRI datasets.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “we aggregated 123,984 MRI scans, across more than 100 primary studies…See Supplementary Information 19 for details on all primary studies contributing to the reference dataset, including multiple publicly available open MRI datasets 32-42.”

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: The study performs secondary analysis of previously collected, heterogeneous datasets rather than acquiring new MRI data, so acquisition protocols of primary studies are outside the scope of this paper.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: “deemed not to require…oversight as it consists of secondary analysis of de-identified primary datasets.”

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: They indicate use of preprocessing pipeline categories in the model and describe quality control combining expert visual curation with automated metrics, but do not provide detailed preprocessing steps or specific software pipelines in the main text.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: “image quality control, which used a combination of expert visual curation and automated metrics of image quality (Supplementary Information 2)”; “software version used for pre-processing (five categories)…age, preprocessing pipeline and study were each included in the GAMLSS model estimation…”

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: Model reliability was evaluated with cross-validation and bootstrap resampling; they also performed jack-knife/leave-one-study-out analyses showing N>100 is sufficient for stable out-of-sample estimation.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: “The reliability of the models was assessed and endorsed by cross-validation and bootstrap resampling procedures (Supplementary Information 3).” and “Extensive jack-knife and leave-one-study-out analyses indicated that a study size of N > 100 scans was sufficient for stable and unbiased estimation of out-of-sample centile scores.”

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They report applying the normative model to new MRI studies via out-of-sample estimation and assessing bias/reliability with leave-one-study-out analyses for studies of at least 100 scans, indicating evaluation on independent datasets.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: “A key challenge for brain charts is the accurate centile scoring of out-of-sample MRI data…Extensive jack-knife and leave-one-study-out analyses indicated that a study size of N > 100 scans was sufficient for stable and unbiased estimation of out-of-sample centile scores.” and “Bias and reliability of out-of-sample centile scoring was extensively assessed…for ‘new’ studies comprising at least 100 scans.”

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The paper describes using generalized additive models for location, scale and shape (GAMLSS), outlines the distributional parameters, sex stratification, fractional polynomial age terms, and study-level random effects.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: “We created brain charts…using generalized additive models for location, scale and shape (GAMLSS)…We used GAMLSS to estimate…allowing for random effects…age, preprocessing pipeline and study were each included in the GAMLSS model estimation of first order (μ) and second order (σ) distribution parameters of a generalized gamma distribution using fractional polynomials…”

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: They state that reliability was assessed via cross-validation, bootstrap resampling, and leave-one-study-out analyses for out-of-sample scoring, but specific quantitative performance metrics (e.g., error rates or variance explained) are not reported in the main text.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “The reliability of the models was assessed and endorsed by cross-validation and bootstrap resampling procedures (Supplementary Information 3).” and “Extensive jack-knife and leave-one-study-out analyses indicated that a study size of N > 100 scans was sufficient for stable and unbiased estimation of out-of-sample centile scores.”

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: Although cross-validation and bootstrap procedures are mentioned, the paper does not report sample sizes or demographic characteristics for any training/validation/test partitions of the reference cohort.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: “The reliability of the models was assessed and endorsed by cross-validation and bootstrap resampling procedures…” (no accompanying details on partition sizes or demographics).

nm11_reproducibility.reason: They provide an interactive tool for exploring models and explicitly state that code and models are openly available on GitHub and brainchart.io.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: “We have provided an interactive tool (www.brainchart.io) and made our code and models openly available (https://github.com/brainchart/Lifespan).”

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: The study includes multiple clinical diagnostic groups in the aggregated dataset, but the main text does not describe eligibility criteria, diagnostic standards, or image-quality exclusion criteria for those clinical participants.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: “Relative to the control group (CN), there were highly significant differences in centile scores across…cases diagnosed with multiple disorders…see Supplementary Tables 3, 4…”

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses compare centile scores across diagnostic groups, but no clinical covariates beyond diagnosis (e.g., medication, illness duration, symptom severity) are described or modeled.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: “Case-control differences in centile scores were analysed with a bootstrapped…ANOVA…Pairwise…comparisons…across clinical conditions” (no mention of clinical covariates).

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical data are drawn from the same aggregated set of >100 primary studies covering multiple disorders, with sources detailed in Supplementary Information 19.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: “we aggregated 123,984 MRI scans…from 101,457 human participants…See Supplementary Information 19 for details on all primary studies contributing to the reference dataset…” and “Relative to the control group (CN), there were…cases diagnosed with multiple disorders (Fig. 4a…).”

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: They report that diagnostic groups include large case samples (e.g., N > 500) and show age span across the lifespan, but the main text lacks detailed demographic or clinical descriptors for each clinical cohort.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: “Relative to the control group (CN), there were highly significant differences in centile scores across large (N > 500) groups of cases diagnosed with multiple disorders (Fig. 4a, Supplementary Information 10)…Across all major epochs of the lifespan…the CMD was consistently greater in cases relative to controls…”

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: The paper does not describe diagnostic assessment tools or symptom rating scales used to define clinical groups; only diagnostic labels are referenced.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: “Relative to the control group (CN), there were…cases diagnosed with multiple disorders (Fig. 4a, Supplementary Information 10)” (no assessment methods described).

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: They explain that centile scores benchmark individual scans against age- and sex-normed distributions, interpret deviations as atypicality, and use CMD to summarize multivariate deviation, but do not provide explicit quantitative thresholds for defining extremes.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: “We computed individualized centile scores that benchmarked each individual scan in the context of normative age-related trends…These centiles represent a novel set of population- and age-standardized clinical phenotypes…Relative to the control group (CN), there were highly significant differences in centile scores across…cases…In addition, we generated a cumulative deviation metric, the centile Mahalanobis distance (CMD), to summarize…atypicality.”
